title: A Verdict for the Inheritance Again
premise: Emrys Iversen, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, receives two letters about the same cold case: one confessing to a fire that killed a wealthy heir, one promising a fortune to whoever finds a witness everyone swears is dead. Following the letters' contradictions through a decaying coastal town, Emrys discovers the 'dead' witness is alive, hidden by the very family that hired her, and that her own erased childhood is entangled with the inheritance. When the true arsonist—her estranged mother's old employer—moves to silence everyone, Emrys must choose between closing the case and exposing herself. She testifies outside any courtroom, publishing the verdict the law refused, and finally claims a belonging she never expected: the witness is her sister.
about_author: Vesper Eastwick is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living. They write mysteries from a houseboat on the Atlantic coast, where they insist the fog improves their memory.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Emrys Iversen, at her desk cataloguing closed cases, receives two envelopes postmarked the same day: one confessing to the 1998 Harrowgate estate fire, one offering money for a witness named only 'M.' Her photographic memory flags a detail—the handwriting on both is identical. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional confidence; the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: The Case That Closed Itself
chapters.summary: Emrys pulls the archived Harrowgate file and discovers it was settled without investigation—flagged closed by her own firm eleven years ago, before she was hired. The payout went to the surviving family, the Ashcombes. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into suspicion; she realizes someone inside her world buried this.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys travels to Greyhollow, the coastal town where the fire happened, and finds the ruins of Harrowgate still standing as a fenced memorial. A local archivist recognizes the confession letter's phrasing—it quotes a coroner's report never made public. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt; she's chasing something real.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Waits
chapters.summary: Emrys interviews Odile Ashcombe, matriarch of the family that collected the insurance, in a house frozen in 1998. Odile is gracious, rehearsed, and lies with perfect fluency—but flinches at the name M. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: predator-and-prey tension; Emrys leaves knowing the family fears a living ghost.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears He's Dead
chapters.summary: Town records list the witness, Marek Voss, as dead—drowned weeks after the fire, body never recovered. But three separate townspeople, unprompted, tell Emrys not to ask about him, each more frightened than the last. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread accumulating; the town itself is complicit or captive.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: A second confession letter arrives at Emrys's office, correcting details from the first—and including a photograph of Emrys entering the Greyhollow archive. Someone is watching her and steering her. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: violation; the investigator has become the investigated.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Emrys's fragmented childhood memories surface unbidden—a burning boathouse, a woman singing, a hand pulling her from the water. She has always assumed these were dreams. POV: Emrys (memory). Emotional beat: vertigo; her own past refuses to stay filed away.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Debt
chapters.summary: The archivist, Pell, admits he leaked the coroner's phrasing years ago to a journalist who then disappeared. He gives Emrys the journalist's notes in exchange for a promise: find out what happened to him too. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; the case now carries other people's grief.

chapters.title: A House of Correct Answers
chapters.summary: Emrys returns to Odile and lays out contradictions from the journalist's notes. Odile's son Cassian intervenes, charming and precise, and offers Emrys a retainer—to investigate the letters' sender, not the fire. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: temptation; the family wants to weaponize her.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Working the journalist's notes, Emrys matches tide charts to the night Marek Voss supposedly drowned and proves no body could have washed out to sea from the reported location. He didn't die there—or wasn't there at all. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: exhilaration; the dead witness is mathematically alive.

chapters.title: The Man Who Feeds Gulls
chapters.summary: Following the tide logic, Emrys finds an old man feeding gulls at a shuttered lighthouse—Marek Voss, alive, half-willing to talk. He tells her he saw who set the fire but that naming them killed the last person who tried. POV: alternating Emrys/Marek. Emotional beat: fragile hope meeting hardened fear.

chapters.title: He Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Marek goes silent when Emrys mentions her own surname—Iversen. He says he knew a girl called Emrys before she had that name, pulled from the water the same night. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: shattering recognition; the case is her origin story.

chapters.title: The Mother Question
chapters.summary: Emrys traces her adoption records and finds her mother worked at Harrowgate as a housekeeper—and was fired the week before the fire, accused of theft she likely didn't commit. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together; her mother was the perfect scapegoat.

chapters.title: Cassian's Offer
chapters.summary: Cassian Ashcombe confronts Emrys with everything he knows about her past, offering to restore her mother's name—in exchange for Marek's location. He reveals the second letter writer is his sister, Lys, who wants the truth out. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: moral corner; every path costs someone.

chapters.title: Lys
chapters.summary: Emrys meets Lys Ashcombe secretly at the ruined boathouse. Lys confesses she wrote both letters—one to confess her family's guilt by proxy, one because she needed someone incorruptible. She believes Marek holds proof their father ordered the fire. POV: Lys. Emotional beat: kinship between two women raised on secrets.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: Marek disappears from the lighthouse hours after agreeing to testify. Signs point to Cassian's men. Emrys's firm, pressured by the Ashcombes' lawyers, suspends her license. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: everything stripped away; she is now outside the law entirely.

chapters.title: What Photographic Memory Is For
chapters.summary: Emrys reconstructs, from pure recall, every document, conversation, and detail of the case into a single evidentiary narrative—the verdict no court will hear. She mails copies to journalists, the insurer's board, and the town. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolve; memory becomes testimony.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Fire
chapters.summary: Cassian burns the boathouse—where Lys waits—with Emrys inside range. Emrys drags Lys out through the smoke, reliving the fire from her childhood in reverse: this time she is the hand pulling someone from the flames. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: climax; terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Verdict Outside the Courtroom
chapters.summary: With Marek found alive in Cassian's custody and returned by a guilty deputy, the published evidence forces a reopened investigation. Cassian is arrested; Odile, choosing her daughter over her son, corroborates the timeline. POV: multiple. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Name Before
chapters.summary: Marek gives Emrys her original name and her mother's last letter, kept for twenty-five years. Her mother didn't abandon her—she hid her, then lost her to the system. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: mourning and repair; the past rewritten accurately at last.

chapters.title: Sisters
chapters.summary: Emrys and Lys sit on the rebuilt boathouse steps, comparing childhoods split by the same crime. Lys asks if Emrys will close the file. Emrys says some cases aren't meant to be closed—only carried well. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: quiet belonging; family chosen through truth.

chapters.title: A Verdict for the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys, reinstated and changed, takes a new case—but keeps the Harrowgate file open on her desk, a reminder of what investigation is for. The final image: two letters framed side by side, confession and promise, both fulfilled. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance retained; the story closes like a hand letting go.
